chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I hear the speech from you and I want to narrate it exactly as I heard it from you, but it does not come (exactly).' He said: 'Do you do that deliberately?' I said: 'No.' So he said: 'Do you intend (to preserve) the meanings?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then there is no problem.'

key_terms.الكلام: Speech, discourse — the exact wording of the Imam's statements
key_terms.المعاني: The meanings/purport — the substantive content as opposed to exact wording
key_terms.لا بأس: No problem/harm — a technical jurisprudential formula granting permissibility

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq permit narrating hadiths by meaning rather than exact wording?
ai.summary: Dawood ibn Farqad, a companion of Imam al-Sadiq, asked about the permissibility of narrating hadiths by meaning (riwayah bil-ma'na) when one cannot recall the exact wording. The Imam first inquired whether the imprecision was deliberate, establishing that intent matters in hadith transmission. Upon learning that Dawood's intent was faithful preservation of meaning, the Imam granted permission, affirming that narration by meaning is acceptable when the transmitter is sincere and the semantic content is preserved.
